correctness.rationale: All n<=5 are treated analytically by support size and the only remaining (3,1,1) five-cycle cases, so no computational leap supports minimality. On n>=6 with two nonadjacent singleton taxa the common label A is present in all windows m>=2. Uniform cyclic starts give per-taxon detection p_B=p_C=m/n; the exact joint inclusion count is (m-s)_++(m-n+s)_+, yielding the three-point law and exact variance. For m=floor(n/2), its count ranges sharply between 0 and m-2. Direct enumeration corroborates all 75 set partitions through n=5, both n=6 witness histograms, 18,970 exact distribution/variance cases for n<=40 and the extremal family through n=60; none is used as an infinite proof. The theorem is restricted to cyclic, single-label-per-site, contiguous-window sampling.

originality.rationale: The general separation between spatial mean richness and spatial variability is known (Laurie–Perrier 2007), so novelty is limited to the sharp n=6 full-curve identifiability threshold and an explicit all-n family with identical species-by-species detection curves but a sharp half-window variance spread tending to one. Full relevant source text (2007 and 2008) and semantically related research records were compared at the level of implications. Residual unidentified cyclic-word literature is possible; no independent review is implied.
residual_risks: The exact cyclic-word claim could appear under combinatorics-on-words, coverage, or ecological sliding-window terminology not indexed in the inspected records.
The full body of Scheiner (2003) and all possible historical spatial-ecology references were not independently audited; the relevant 2007 and 2008 primary technical texts were inspected.
Cyclic periodic boundaries and single-occupancy sites are idealizations; empirical relevance requires matching the field sampling design.

value.rationale: Species-area mean curves are often used to summarize spatial biodiversity; even their species-by-species decomposition fails to encode pairwise spatial co-detection. The result finds the exact first possible landscape size for this nonidentifiability and an unrestricted analytically maximal within-family variance discrepancy approaching the largest possible variance for a random variable supported on the three richness levels 1,2,3 with mean 2. In even-sized far configurations, half-window richness is constant while the nearby-singleton pattern approaches equal probabilities at richness 1 and 3. This is a nontrivial, motivated identifiability boundary with implications for sampling-risk summaries, not just a table recomputation.
